question: Why does a zipper snag on invisible fabric?
why_curious: When you’re in a hurry, a zipper can suddenly get stuck on a seam you can’t see—just a few inches of fabric.  It feels like a glitch, but the physics of friction, tooth geometry, and tiny hidden fibers all conspire to make the zipper jam.  Understanding why this happens reveals how everyday design choices can create hidden frustrations.
curiosity_gap: People think a zipper will glide smoothly over any seam, but hidden micro‑textures and friction coefficients actually cause it to get stuck.
